# Jonah Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 341r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JON_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** And-it-was-evil [vayyera] to Yonah a-great evil [ra'ah gedolah], and-it-burned [vayyichar] to-him.

**4:2** And-he-prayed [vayyitpallel] to YHWH and-said, "Please [ana], YHWH, was-not this my-word [devari] while-I-was upon my-land [admati]? Therefore [al-ken] I-fled-before [qiddameti livroach] to-Tarshish, for I-knew [yadati] that you [are] a-God [El] gracious [channun] and-compassionate [verachum], slow [erekh] of-anger [appayim] and-great [rav] of-loyalty [chesed], and-relenting [venicham] concerning-the-evil [ha-ra'ah]."

**4:3** "And-now, YHWH, take [qach], please [na], my-life [nafshi] from-me, for better [tov] [is] my-death [moti] than-my-life [me-chayyai]."

**4:4** And-said YHWH, "Is-it-good [ha-heitev] that-it-burns [charah] to-you?"

**4:5** And-went-out [vayyetse] Yonah from the-city and-sat [vayyeshev] to-the-east [mi-qedem] of-the-city, and-made [vayyaas] for-himself there a-booth [sukkah], and-sat [vayyeshev] under-it [tachteyha] in-the-shade [ba-tsel], until [ad] he-would-see [yir'eh] what would-happen [yihyeh] in-the-city.

**4:6** And-appointed [vayman] YHWH God a-plant [qiqayon] and-caused-it-to-go-up [vayyaal] over Yonah to-be shade [tsel] over his-head [rosho], to-deliver-him [lehatsil lo] from-his-evil [me-ra'ato]. And-rejoiced [vayyismach] Yonah over the-plant [ha-qiqayon] a-great joy [simchah gedolah].

**4:7** And-appointed [vayman] the-God a-worm [tola'at] at-the-rising [ba-alot] of-the-dawn [ha-shachar] the-next-day [le-mocharat], and-it-struck [vatakh] the-plant and-it-withered [vayyivash].

**4:8** And-it-was at-the-rising [ki-zroach] of-the-sun, and-appointed [vayman] God a-scorching [charishit] east [qadim] wind [ruach], and-struck [vatakh] the-sun upon the-head [rosh] of-Yonah, and-he-fainted [vayyit'allaf]. And-he-asked [vayyish'al] his-soul [nafsho] to-die [lamut] and-said, "Better [tov] [is] my-death [moti] than-my-life [me-chayyai]."

**4:9** And-said God to Yonah, "Is-it-good [ha-heitev] that-it-burns [charah] to-you over the-plant [ha-qiqayon]?" And-he-said, "It-burns [charah] to-me well [heitev] — unto death [ad-mavet]."

**4:10** And-said YHWH, "You had-pity [chasta] on the-plant which you-did-not labor [lo amalta] over-it and-did-not grow [lo giddalta] it, which [as] a-son [bin] of-a-night [lailah] it-came [hayah] and-[as] a-son of-a-night it-perished [avad]."

**4:11** "And-I, shall-I-not have-pity [lo achus] on Nineveh, the-city the-great, in-which there-are more [harbeh] than-twelve ten-thousand [shtem-esreh ribbo] persons [adam] who do-not know [lo yade'u] between their-right-hand [yeminam] and-their-left-hand [le-semolam], and-beasts [behemah] many [rabbah]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — The creedal formula:** Jonah quotes Exodus 34:6-7 — the foundational self-revelation of YHWH. But he quotes it as a *complaint*. The attributes that Israel celebrates (gracious, compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loyalty) are precisely what Jonah resents. He *knew* God would forgive Nineveh — and that is exactly why he ran.

**v.6 — "plant" (qiqayon):** The *qiqayon* is usually identified as the castor-oil plant (*Ricinus communis*), known for rapid growth. Jerome's translation as *hedera* ("ivy") in the Vulgate sparked a famous dispute with Augustine.

**v.11 — "twelve ten-thousand":** 120,000 people "who do not know their right hand from their left" — usually understood as young children or as a hyperbolic description of moral ignorance. The final word of the book is *rabbah* ("many") — the book ends not with Jonah's response but with God's unanswered question.

*— EMET*
